Using \( \sin x = \operatorname{Im}(e^{ix}) \),

\[
\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-x}\sin x\,dx
= \operatorname{Im}\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-(1-i)x}\,dx
= \operatorname{Im}\left(\frac{2}{(1-i)^3}\right).
\]

Now \((1-i)^3 = -2-2i\), so

\[
\frac{2}{(1-i)^3} = \frac{2}{-2-2i} = -\frac{1}{1+i} = -\frac{1-i}{2} = -\frac12 + \frac12 i.
\]

Thus the imaginary part is \(\frac12\).
